title: TestCase
description:
The TestCase class represents a single test. This class is only available in the main thread. Refer to the "Runner API" if you are working with runtime tasks.

The TestCase instance always has a type property with the value of test. You can use it to distinguish between different task types:

entries.name: TestCase
entries.description:
The TestCase class represents a single test. This class is only available in the main thread. Refer to the "Runner API" if you are working with runtime tasks.

The TestCase instance always has a type property with the value of test. You can use it to distinguish between different task types:

children.name: project
children.description: This references the TestProject that the test belongs to.

children.name: module
children.description: This is a direct reference to the TestModule where the test is defined.

children.name: name
children.description: This is a test name that was passed to the test function.

children.name: fullName
children.description: The name of the test including all parent suites separated with > symbol. This test has a full name "the validation logic > the validation works correctly":

children.name: id
children.description:
This is test's unique identifier. This ID is deterministic and will be the same for the same test across multiple runs. The ID is based on the project name, module ID and test order.

The ID looks like this:

examples.code:
1223128da3_0_0
^^^^^^^^^^ the file hash
           ^ suite index
             ^ test index

notes: DANGERDon't try to parse the ID. It can have a minus at the start: -1223128da3_0_0_0.

children.name: location
children.description:
The location in the module where the test was defined. Locations are collected only if includeTaskLocation is enabled in the config. Note that this option is automatically enabled if --reporter=html, --ui or --browser flags are used.

The location of this test will be equal to { line: 3, column: 1 }:

children.name: parent
children.description: Parent suite. If the test was called directly inside the module, the parent will be the module itself.

children.name: options
children.description: The options that test was collected with.
signatures:
interface TaskOptions {
  readonly each: boolean | undefined
  readonly fails: boolean | undefined
  readonly concurrent: boolean | undefined
  readonly shuffle: boolean | undefined
  readonly retry: number | undefined
  readonly repeats: number | undefined
  readonly tags: string[] | undefined
  readonly timeout: number | undefined
  readonly mode: 'run' | 'only' | 'skip' | 'todo'
}

examples.code:

children.name: tags 4.1.0+
children.description: Tags that were implicitly or explicitly assigned to the test.

children.name: ok
children.description: Checks if the test did not fail the suite. If the test is not finished yet or was skipped, it will return true.

examples.code: function ok(): boolean

children.name: meta
children.description:
Custom metadata that was attached to the test during its execution. The meta can be attached by assigning a property to the ctx.task.meta object during a test run:

If the test did not finish running yet, the meta will be an empty object, unless it has static meta:

Since Vitest 4.1, Vitest inherits meta property defined on the suite.

examples.code: function meta(): TaskMeta
test('the validation works correctly', { meta: { decorated: true } })

children.name: result
children.description:
Test results. If test is not finished yet or was just collected, it will be equal to TestResultPending:

If the test was skipped, the return value will be TestResultSkipped:

If the test failed, the return value will be TestResultFailed:

If the test passed, the return value will be TestResultPassed:

examples.code: function result(): TestResult

notes: TIPIf the test was skipped because another test has only flag, the options.mode will be equal to skip.
WARNINGNote that the test with passed state can still have errors attached - this can happen if retry was triggered at least once.

children.name: diagnostic
children.description: Useful information about the test like duration, memory usage, etc:
signatures:
interface TestDiagnostic {
  /**
   * If the duration of the test is above `slowTestThreshold`.
   */
  readonly slow: boolean
  /**
   * The amount of memory used by the test in bytes.
   * This value is only available if the test was executed with `logHeapUsage` flag.
   */
  readonly heap: number | undefined
  /**
   * The time it takes to execute the test in ms.
   */
  readonly duration: number
  /**
   * The time in ms when the test started.
   */
  readonly startTime: number
  /**
   * The amount of times the test was retried.
   */
  readonly retryCount: number
  /**
   * The amount of times the test was repeated as configured by `repeats` option.
   * This value can be lower if the test failed during the repeat and no `retry` is configured.
   */
  readonly repeatCount: number
  /**
   * If test passed on a second retry.
   */
  readonly flaky: boolean
}

examples.code: function diagnostic(): TestDiagnostic | undefined

notes: INFOdiagnostic() will return undefined if the test was not scheduled to run yet.
